newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GST key to Australian tax reform - Kennett.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GST key to Australian tax reform - Kennett.

text.p: Victoria state Premier Jeff Kennett said on Monday the federal government should undertake taxation reform after the next national election, advocating a consumer tax as a key reform.

"I am just hopeful and I genuinely believe and hope that whoever wins the next federal election -- and I believe that will be the conservative side of politics -- then tax reform is a non-negotiable option to follow immediately on that election," Kennett told Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.
"Obviously there has got to be a consumer tax of some scale and that has got to be the linchpin of any reform," he said.
Prime Minister John Howard has previously said he would not introduce a value-added consumption tax, such as a goods and services tax (GST), in this term of parliament.
The Liberal-National government has also said it would not introduce new taxes during its current three year term in office.
